Customer obsession, no matter how big you become.

At Primary Venture Partners 9th NYC Tech Summit, Etched co-founder and CEO Gavin Uberti credited TSMC’s relentless service as a major reason it wins. A trillion-dollar company, still willing to experiment and adapt to help a small customer succeed.

I really enjoyed his session. His examples came from hardware, but the company-building lessons apply much more broadly.

⚡️ Great day at the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara! Team Synopsys hosted a startup panel “Build a Winning AI Chip Startup from Scratch,” featuring cutting-edge co-founders and leaders - Robert W. from Etched, Andy Hock from Cerebras, Jonathan Pearce from AheadComputing, Usman Ali, Ph.D. from Meta, and moderated by Sandeep Mehndiratta from Synopsys Inc. 💡 The most compelling part of the conversations was hearing the real challenges they faced—and overcame—building and scaling AI chip businesses in a rapidly evolving era. Thank you to Primary Venture Partners for the invite to today's NY Summit. Every talk I listened to had 🤯 or 💡 moments. Some takeouts:

From Etched: the entire AI revolution is still fundamentally constrained by a lack of compute. Lots of smart people are working on solving this
From Jeanne DeWitt Grosser: slightly counter-intuitively, the greatest value of AI in the workplace is in making more time for human to human relationships, by automating drudgery. "Time with customer" should perhaps become a KPI 
Parallel Web Systems is building web search and browsing for agents from the ground up. The agentic internet is in its infancy but growing very fast

Primary Venture Partners Summit is like back to school for NYC VC. It's great to see the out of towners, but for the NYC ecosystem it feels like a reunion. Frankly I spent most of the time catching up with LPs, GPs and founders, but did hear a few presentations. Topics were pretty far reaching. Will AI end humanity? That one I'm going to let play out.
 Gavin Uberti, Etched Patrick O'Shaughnessy, Colossus

Particularly enjoyed the most human of panels with Lance Armstrong. He was "fired from the world", and the work has been going on ever since. A nonlinear life. Some lines that stuck:

7506327376478404608.author: Jessica Radow
7506327376478404608.text:
NYC was looking particularly good yesterday! Perfect weather and even better tech momentum!

Great day at Primary Venture Partners NYC Tech Summit. Exciting to see so many founders, investors, and operators  coming together in one place.

Truly a treat to hear from so many incredible founders Gavin Uberti, Matthew Prince, Cristóbal Valenzuela, Dan Shipper, Evan Beard, including the legendary Lance Armstrong, with conversations spanning AI and compute to robotics, and the broader reindustrialization happening in the US.

Let's keep it going! And thank you again to the awesome Primary Venture Partners team!

Radical Ventures has raised more than US$1 billion for its new Breakouts AI fund, expanding its focus toward later-stage AI companies requiring larger amounts of capital to scale talent, computing and infrastructure. The fund has initially allocated capital to 12 companies, highlighting the growing scale of private AI financing.

• Radical Ventures has raised more than US$1 billion for Breakouts, which the firm says is the largest venture fund raised in Canada.

7506410014555770880.author: Joshua Scott
7506410014555770880.text:
I have had a week to recover from Ideas Fest now, a full week was certainly needed.

It was incredible to finally get Etched Tech properly out in the wild. (If you can call Tring wild!)

We had a brilliant setup with CMS in a slightly over-the-top, yet suave, Moroccan-style tent, which turned out to be a pretty great place to talk to founders about ideas, ownership and how messy the early stages of building something often are.

Being able to demo Etched live was probably the highlight for me. There’s a big difference between explaining what the product does and watching people see their own use cases in it straight away.
